The evidence indicates that retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) does not consistently improve the factual accuracy of LLM-generated answers; results vary significantly depending on the benchmark, metric, and specific implementation, with some studies showing improvements, others showing no measurable change, and several showing decreases in accuracy or increases in hallucination.

**Evidence of Improvement:**
Several studies report that RAG improves factual accuracy or reduces hallucination rates:
*   On LawFactQA, the retrieval-augmented model had a lower hallucination rate (17.8%) compared to the parametric-only model (29.5%) [S001, 1932-2086].
*   On LawFactQA, the variant reading retrieved evidence had a higher fraction of factually correct answers (57.1%) compared to the generator without document access (50.5%) [S002, 2153-2269].
*   On PopCultureQA, the RAG pipeline had a lower hallucination rate (18.3%) than the vanilla LLM (21.5%) [S006, 2189-2326].
*   On SciFactBench, the retrieval-augmented generator had a significantly lower hallucination rate (6.3%) than the vanilla LLM (20.2%) [S008, 2598-2656].
*   On TriviaCheck, the retrieve-then-read model achieved higher fact-level accuracy (67.6%) than the closed-book model (54.3%) [S011, 2088-2251].
*   On HistoryQuest, the retrieval-augmented generator had a lower hallucination frequency (5.1%) than the no-retrieval baseline (10.3%) [S016, 2303-2484].
*   On PopCultureQA, the system grounded in retrieved passages had a lower fraction of invented facts (31.4%) than the language model used on its own (39.2%) [S017, 2404-2664].
*   On a general benchmark, the retrieve-then-read model had a lower hallucination rate (16.3%) than the vanilla LLM (20.8%) [S018, 2705-2760].
*   On LawFactQA, the retrieval-augmented model had higher answer accuracy (64.6%) than the no-retrieval baseline (52.3%) [S020, 2556-2737].

**Evidence of No Measurable Improvement:**
Other studies found that RAG did not make answers measurably more accurate:
*   On LawFactQA, the retrieval-augmented model had a slightly lower fact-level accuracy (77.4%) than the parametric-only model (78.3%) [S003, 3089-3145].
*   On LawFactQA, the retrieve-then-read model scored 0.9 percentage points lower in answer accuracy than the parametric-only model [S004, 3015-3143].
*   On OpenFactQA, the configuration looking up supporting documents had a higher share of unsupported statements (39.9%) than the generator without document access (39.1%) [S007, 2721-3019].
*   On TriviaCheck, the retrieval-augmented model had a lower hallucination rate (32.3%) than the vanilla LLM (38.1%), but the study concluded that adding retrieved documents left the amount of hallucinated content essentially unchanged [S010, 2143-2285, 2739-3031].
*   On SciFactBench, the RAG pipeline had higher answer accuracy (66.1%) than the parametric-only model (62.5%), but the study concluded that adding retrieved documents left the correctness of the answers essentially unchanged [S015, 2610-2777, 3357-3595].
*   On TriviaCheck, the retrieve-then-read model scored 0.8 percentage points lower in fact-level accuracy than the no-retrieval baseline [S019, 2581-2715].
*   On LawFactQA, the retrieval-augmented model had higher answer accuracy (64.6%) than the no-retrieval baseline (52.3%), but the study concluded that adding retrieved documents left the correctness of the answers essentially unchanged [S020, 2556-2737, 3387-3674].

**Evidence of Decreased Accuracy or Increased Hallucination:**
Some studies report that RAG made answers less accurate or increased hallucination:
*   On NewsTruthQA and LawFactQA, the RAG pipeline had lower fact-level accuracy than the parametric-only model (e.g., 40.7% vs 49.9% on LawFactQA) [S009, 2474-2750].
*   On NewsTruthQA, the variant reading retrieved evidence had a higher share of unsupported statements (29.2%) than the model answering from its own parameters (19.3%) [S012, 2463-2752].
*   On a popular culture benchmark, the retrieval-augmented generator had lower answer accuracy (40.3%) than the vanilla LLM (47.5%) [S013, 3173-3242].
*   On BioClaimQA and TriviaCheck, the retrieval-augmented model had lower answer accuracy than the closed-book model (e.g., 53.5% vs 60.6% on BioClaimQA) [S014, 1788-2254].

In summary, while RAG can improve factual accuracy in some contexts, the evidence is mixed, with many studies showing no significant benefit or even a decline in performance.
